### The Prophecy of Amos
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/prophecy-amos
Passage: Amos 1:1
Points:
- Amos was an ordinary agricultural worker rather than a lifelong prophet or member of the religious elite.
- God called him to travel north to deliver warnings during a period of significant geopolitical expansion.
- National wealth and security led the ruling classes to exploit the poor and boast in their own power.
- Times of material success often tempt people to rely on themselves rather than on the Lord.
- Christians must guard against self-reliance and use whatever influence they possess to serve others.

### The Lord of All Nations
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-august-14-2025.html
Passage: Amos 1:2, 4-5
Points:
- God sees all human conduct and will ultimately settle all accounts with perfect justice.
- The Lord strongly condemns human trafficking, unchecked violence, and treating people made in His image as property.
- Believers can find deep comfort knowing that no injustice they suffer escapes God's notice.
- Divine judgment against ancient nations warns us to examine our own hearts for anger, greed, and selfishness.
- Followers of Christ can repent of sin without fear because Jesus bore our punishment at Calvary.

### Devotional: Amos 1
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/2-kings-25-hebrews-7-amos-1-psalm-144/
Passage: Amos 1:1-15
Points:
- Amos was not a professional prophet or priest but an ordinary shepherd sent across borders to preach.
- Israel's political stability and economic prosperity under Jeroboam II concealed serious moral decay and idolatry.
- The description of the Lord roaring like a lion indicates that divine patience has reached its limit.
- The numerical formula highlights that the repeated sins of these nations have piled up to judgment.
- God's rebukes of neighboring nations demonstrate that He reigns as the sovereign Judge over all the earth.
